sections.heading: Function
paragraphs: LMO7 is responsible for converting 5-methylcytosine (5mC) to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), which is responsible for initiating active DNA demethylation [Ketchum et al., 2024].

paragraphs.text: Our cohort analysis discovers the case(s) in rare frequency that LMO7 is disturbed as shown here.

sections.heading: Literature
paragraphs: In several cancer models, loss or dysregulation of LMO7 can alter cell morphology, migration, invasion, and EMT-associated programs [Zhen et al., 2022, Zeng et al., 2024, Liu et al., 2021].

paragraphs.text: Our analysis discovers the case(s) in rare frequency that demonstrates the oligogenic interaction involving LMO7.
paragraphs.suffix: to see the co-occurring SVs that are appearing with LMO7 in our curated palatogenesis pathway diagram. It shows the involvement of developmental enhancers via the TET-SNAIL4-BMP axis.
